== Biography ==

'''Archibald Glasgow''' was baptised on '''19 June 1614''' at Glasgow High Kirk. He was recorded as the lawful son of [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]] and [[Stewart-65226|Margaret Steuart]]. William Howie, Michael Broune and Andrew Mylne were named in the baptismal entry.<ref>Glasgow High Kirk Baptisms 1609–1777, vol. 1/1329.</ref>

He graduated '''Master of Arts''' from the University of Glasgow in '''1635'''.<ref>University of Glasgow, University Story, “Archibaldus Glasgua,” graduate, Master of Arts, 1635. https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/people?search=&surname=Glas&forename=</ref>

== Probable Identification in County Donegal ==

A series of Irish records concerns a clergyman named '''Archibald Glasgow''' who was active in County Donegal between approximately 1641 and 1677.

The records form a geographically and chronologically coherent clerical career and probably concern one man. The uncommon name, chronology and clerical background also create a strong circumstantial case that this was the Archibald Glasgow baptised in Glasgow in 1614 and educated at the University of Glasgow.

No inspected Irish record, however, explicitly identifies the Donegal clergyman as:

* the son of George Glasgow and Margaret Steuart;
* a native of Glasgow;
* the man baptised at Glasgow High Kirk in 1614; or
* the University of Glasgow graduate of 1635.

The identification should therefore be treated as probable rather than conclusively proved.

Records concerning the Irish Archibald include:

* An '''Archibald Glasgow''' serving as rector of '''Killea, County Donegal''', in or before 1641, with later restoration in 1661.<ref>Ulster Plantation and Migration project, person record for Archibald Glasgow. https://ulster-settlers.maynoothuniversity.ie/people/32084</ref>
* A clergyman of that name associated with '''Faughanvale''' in 1654 and '''Taboyne''' in 1660.<ref>Ulster Plantation and Migration project, person record for Archibald Glasgow. https://ulster-settlers.maynoothuniversity.ie/people/32084</ref>
* An Archibald Glasgow possibly mentioned in a 1657 disciplinary record concerning drunkenness.<ref>Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland. https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/IMC-AH-15-1944-MacLysaght</ref>
* A cleric named '''Archibald Glasgow''' appointed rector and vicar of '''Clondevadock, Tullyfern and Aughnish''' in County Donegal in April 1661.<ref>James Seaton Reid, ''A History of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland'', 1853, p. 278. https://en.geneanet.org/archives/ouvrages?action=detail&book_type=livre&livre_id=6279357&page=278</ref>
* An '''Archibald Glasgow''' appearing in a County Donegal Hearth Money Roll dated 1665.<ref>Virtual Record Treasury of Ireland, TCD MS 6232. https://www.virtualtreasury.ie/item/TCD-MS-6232</ref>
* '''Archibald Glasgow of Ramelton, County Donegal''', named as obligee in a bond from William Dutton of Greenforte dated 1675/76.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1825/A/2, bond from William Dutton of Greenforte to Archibald Glasgow of Ramelton, 1675/76.</ref>
* '''Archibald Glasgow of Rathmalton, County Donegal, clerk''', whose prerogative will was proved in '''1677'''.<ref>Sir Arthur Vicars, ''Index to the Prerogative Wills of Ireland, 1536–1810'', entry for Archibald Glasgow, clerk, Rathmalton, County Donegal, 1677. https://archive.org/details/indextoprerogati00vica</ref>
* A separate probate-index transcription records '''Archibald Glascoe of Rathmatton, County Donegal''', in '''1679'''.<ref>Irish probate index transcription supplied July 2026, entry for Archibald Glascoe, Rathmatton, County Donegal, 1679.</ref>

“Rathmalton” was an historical spelling associated with Rathmelton or Ramelton. “Rathmatton” in the 1679 transcription is probably a spelling or transcription variant of the same place. These names should not be confused with Rathmullan.

The Archibald named in the 1675/76 Ramelton bond and the Rathmalton clergyman whose will was proved in 1677 were almost certainly the same person. The uncommon name, occupation, place and close dates strongly support that conclusion.

The 1679 entry probably represents a duplicate index entry, a later probate action or a transcription of the same estate rather than a second local Archibald Glasgow. The two-year discrepancy has not been resolved and should not be silently merged into a single probate date.

If the Donegal clergyman was the man baptised in Glasgow in 1614, he died before probate was granted in 1677, aged approximately 62 or 63. Ramelton was his recorded residence, but it has not been established as his place of death.

== Wife and Children ==

No wife or child has yet been identified from an inspected primary record.

The existence of Archibald’s 1677 prerogative will is potentially important. The original will was probably among the records destroyed in Dublin in 1922, but a pre-destruction genealogical abstract may survive in the notebooks compiled by Sir William Betham.

Such an abstract may identify:

* Archibald’s wife;
* sons or daughters;
* married daughters or sons-in-law;
* siblings;
* executors;
* other legatees; or
* property inherited by his heirs.

The separate 1679 entry should also be investigated to determine whether it represents a duplicate, a later grant, an administration or another action concerning the same estate.

Until a will abstract or another direct record is examined, no spouse or child should be attached to this profile.

== Possible Connection to Thomas Glasgow ==

No record has been found proving that Archibald was the father, brother or other close relative of Thomas Glasgow of Ballindrait, Shannon or Lifford.

Thomas Glasgow was described as being of '''Lifford, County Donegal''', and as an esquire, in connection with the 1689 attainder proceedings. His transactions also place him within the same broad Donegal landholding network as Abraham and James Creighton.

The chronology allows Thomas to have been Archibald’s son, nephew or younger brother, but this is speculation. Archibald’s 1675/76 bond names only Archibald Glasgow and William Dutton and gives no family relationship.

Neither the 1677 nor the 1679 probate-index entry supplies the contents of Archibald’s will or names any beneficiary.

The PRONI catalogue descriptions for Thomas Glasgow’s known transactions likewise name Thomas, Abraham Creighton and James Creighton, but do not identify Thomas’s parents, wife, children, heirs or siblings:

* D1939/18/8/1
* D1939/18/1/3
* D1939/18/3/25
* D1939/18/7/1
* D1939/18/11/16

The full deeds may contain witnesses, recitals, endorsements or inheritance language omitted from the catalogue descriptions.

== Possible Connection to Nathaniel Glasgow ==

No record has been found proving that Archibald was an ancestor or other relative of [[Glasgow-1137|Nathaniel Glasgow]].

The proposed descent:

Archibald Glasgow
|
?
|
Thomas Glasgow of Ballindrait/Shannon/Lifford
|
?
|
Nathaniel Glasgow

remains chronologically and geographically possible, but unsupported by direct kinship evidence.

Neither Archibald’s bond nor the available descriptions of Thomas’s transactions name Nathaniel. Nathaniel’s university record also names no father.

== Other Proposed Relationships ==

A possible relationship with [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow (1614–)]], who married Bessie Howie, has previously been suggested because the surname Howie appears in Archibald’s baptismal entry.

The presence of the same surname is insufficient to establish that Archibald and William were brothers or cousins. William Howie was named in Archibald’s baptismal entry, but the record does not state that he was a relative.

A connection with [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow (c.1533–)]], a burgess and property owner in Glasgow, has also been proposed. The suggested great-uncle and grand-nephew relationship depends upon several reconstructed parent-child links that have not been established from contemporary records.

These relationships should remain research hypotheses.

== Research Priorities ==

The most important unresolved record is the genealogical abstract of Archibald’s 1677 will, if it survives among the Betham notebooks.

Other useful records would include:

* the underlying source for the 1679 Archibald Glascoe probate-index entry;
* records explaining whether the 1679 entry was a duplicate, later grant or administration;
* the complete document for PRONI D1825/A/2;
* complete copies of Thomas Glasgow’s five D1939 transactions;
* Raphoe diocesan probate and administration records;
* marriage bonds and licence indexes;
* parish registers for Killea, Ramelton and neighbouring areas;
* property records naming Archibald’s heirs after 1677; and
* original Glasgow baptismal records for other possible children of George Glasgow and Margaret Steuart.

== Research Conclusion ==

The Donegal records from 1641 to 1677 probably document the career of one clergyman, culminating in the 1675/76 Ramelton bond and the probate of the will of Archibald Glasgow of Rathmalton in 1677.

The 1679 entry for Archibald Glascoe of Rathmatton is probably connected with the same estate, but its precise nature remains unresolved.

Identity with the Archibald Glasgow baptised in Glasgow in 1614 and awarded an M.A. in 1635 is a strong chronological and occupational fit. It remains circumstantial because no inspected Irish record names his Scottish parents, birthplace or university.

No spouse, child or proved line of descent to Thomas Glasgow or Nathaniel Glasgow has been identified.

== Biography ==
The date and place of birth of '''Thomas Glasgow''' are unknown. Because he was recorded as an adult in January 1684 and styled an esquire by 1689, he was probably born before about 1671. Lifford may be retained in the structured birth-place field as uncertain because it is his earliest stated locality, but the record does not prove that he was born there. No inspected record identifies his wife, children or parents.

On 22 January 1684 Thomas Glasgow was indexed as defendant in an Exchequer proceeding brought by a Bryson or Brison described as “of Raphoe.”<ref name="Exch1684">National Archives of Ireland, Equity Exchequer Bill Book 1684–1686, vol. 5, p. 102, 22 January 1684; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F007635147%2F00191&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001584141 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001584141&tab=this transcript].</ref>

In 1689 a printed list associated with the Irish attainder legislation named “Thomas Glasgow of Lifford, in the County of Donnegal, Esq.” among Protestants regarded as absent from Ireland or adherents of William of Orange.<ref name="King">''The State of the Protestants of Ireland under the Late King James's Government'', list of persons named in the attainder legislation, [https://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo/a47446.0001.001/1%3A6 p. 275].</ref> This establishes his Lifford association and designation, not his birthplace or ownership of every property later named.

On 2 March 1692 Thomas was a defendant in a Chancery proceeding in which Abraham Creighton was a plaintiff or petitioner.<ref name="Chan1692">National Archives of Ireland, Court of Chancery Bill Book 1692–1696, vol. 11, p. 36, 2 March 1692; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F007635177%2F00507&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F0000106395 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F0000106395&tab=this transcript].</ref>

On 23 December 1692 Thomas entered into a counterpart deed of partition with Colonel Abraham Creighton of Crom, County Fermanagh, and Abraham's son James Creighton concerning Donegal lands.<ref name="Partition1692">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/8/1, counterpart deed of partition, 23 December 1692.</ref>

On 25–26 May 1693 Thomas was described as “of Ballindroight” in a lease and release with Colonel Abraham Creighton concerning lands including Drumloane, Glencosh and Shannon in the Barony of Raphoe.<ref name="Lease1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/1/3, lease and release between Thomas Glasgow, or Glascow, of Ballindroight and Colonel Abraham Creighton, 25–26 May 1693.</ref>

On 26 May 1693 Thomas executed a performance bond and deed of defeasance for £4,000 in favour of Abraham Creighton.<ref name="Bond1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/3/25, bond and deed of defeasance, 26 May 1693.</ref> A counterpart release that day, for £400, concerned lands including Teroneal, Drumlane, Glancosh and Shannon in the Barony of Raphoe.<ref name="Release1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/7/1, counterpart release, 26 May 1693.</ref>

On 26 May 1694 Thomas was described as “of Shannon” when he issued a copy bond for performance of covenants in a release to Abraham Creighton.<ref name="Bond1694">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/11/16, copy bond for performance of covenant, 26 May 1694.</ref>

On 25 November 1695 Thomas appeared in a letter and memorandum concerning a joint bond of £6,000 with Hugh Hamill, Abraham Creighton, John Hamilton and John Johnston, all described as esquires.<ref name="Memo1695">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/3/25, letter and memorandum, 25 November 1695.</ref>

On 15 May 1701 Thomas Glasgow, Esquire, was indexed as plaintiff in an Exchequer bill against John Moffett, William Humphrys, Archibald Sinclair and Margaret Sinclair.<ref name="Exch1701">National Archives of Ireland, Equity Exchequer Bill Book 1700–1701, vol. 12, p. 121, 15 May 1701; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F007635145%2F00152&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001527519 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001527519&tab=this transcript]. The page includes June 1701 procedural annotations.</ref>

The rare surname, Esquire designation, exact Raphoe reference and repeated Abraham Creighton association strongly identify the court litigant with the man of Lifford, Ballindroight and Shannon. Thomas was alive after 15 May 1701. His death date and place remain unknown.

== Identity and Status ==

The references to Thomas Glasgow of '''Lifford''', '''Ballindroight''' and '''Shannon''' almost certainly concern the same man.

The surname was uncommon, the locations were within the same Donegal and Raphoe property network, and the records form a continuous sequence of transactions involving Abraham and James Creighton between 1692 and 1695.

No inspected record explicitly states that the Thomas of Lifford was the same person as the Thomas of Ballindroight or Shannon. The identification is nevertheless strongly supported by the chronology, geography and repeated association with the Creightons.

Thomas was styled '''esquire''' and participated in substantial legal and financial transactions. The bonds, considerations and lands involved show that he was a significant actor in the Donegal property network.

The surviving catalogue descriptions do not establish his precise role in every transaction. Depending upon the instrument, he may have acted as:

* owner;
* purchaser;
* vendor;
* mortgagee;
* trustee;
* tenant;
* surety; or
* another party with a legal interest.

He should therefore be described as an esquire and legal or property actor. The records do not by themselves prove that he beneficially owned every estate or parcel named.

== Family and Relationship Research ==

The available records name Thomas Glasgow, Abraham Creighton, James Creighton and several other parties to the transactions.

They do not identify Thomas’s:

* father or mother;
* wife;
* sons or daughters;
* brothers or sisters;
* heirs;
* executors; or
* other stated relatives.

No family relationship between Thomas and the Creightons is given. Their repeated appearance together establishes a continuing legal and financial association, not kinship.

No inspected record proves that Thomas was a son, brother, nephew or other relative of [[Glasgow-1101|Archibald Glasgow M.A. (1614–bef.1677)]].

The chronology and geography allow Thomas to have been a son or younger relative of the Archibald Glasgow who served as a clergyman in County Donegal and whose will was proved in 1677. That remains a research hypothesis only.

No inspected record proves that Thomas was the father of [[Glasgow-1136|Nathaniel Glasgow M.A. (died 1743)]].

The proposed line:

Archibald Glasgow
|
?
|
Thomas Glasgow of Lifford, Ballindroight and Shannon
|
?
|
Nathaniel Glasgow

remains unsupported by direct kinship evidence. Each question mark represents a missing documentary link.

A '''James Glasgow''' appearing in Killybegs account material in 1728 may belong to an adjacent generation of the Donegal family. The entry does not identify James as Thomas’s son or other relative.

No spouse or child should be attached to Thomas from chronology, geography, naming patterns or unsourced family trees alone.

== Distinction from Other Men Named Thomas Glasgow ==

Thomas should not be identified with [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow]], the child baptised in Scotland in 1612, without evidence connecting that person to Lifford or County Donegal.

A man baptised in 1612 would have been approximately 77 years old in 1689 and over 80 during the property transactions of 1692–1695. That identity is chronologically possible but unlikely and is unsupported by any inspected cross-channel record.

The two profiles should remain separate unless a deed, will, migration record or other contemporary source establishes that they were the same person.

== Death ==

Thomas’s date and place of death are unknown.

He was alive on '''25 November 1695''', when he was named in the memorandum concerning the £6,000 joint bond.

No will, administration, burial entry or record naming his heirs has yet been identified.

His profile should therefore use:

* birth probably before 1671, based on adult status by 1689, with birthplace unknown; and
* death after 25 November 1695, place unknown.

The year 1670 and County Donegal should not be presented as a certain birth date and place without an independent source.

'''Samuel Glasgow''' was born about 1801 in Ireland. Samuel became a merchant at Prescott. The 1851 Canada Directory listed “Glasgow, Samuel, general store, Main st.”<ref>[https://numerique.banq.qc.ca/patrimoine/details/52327/5139192 Robert W. S. Mackay, ''The Canada Directory'' (Montreal, 1851)], Prescott entry for Samuel Glasgow.</ref> In the original 1851 census he was a Presbyterian storekeeper, born in Ireland and aged 51 at his next birthday. All eight were recorded as Presbyterians.<ref name="Census1851" /> Orena's rare name and compatible age recur in a transcription of the 1861 Prescott grammar-school census, where she was associated with Samuel Glasgow, storekeeper.<ref>[https://thepastaroundus.wordpress.com/2015/10/12/black-walnuts-squirrels-and-prescott-high-school/ “Black Walnuts, Squirrels and Prescott High School,” ''The Past Around Us''], 1861 entry for Orena Glasgow, aged 17 (accessed 13 August 2026).</ref>

A descendant's local history says that Samuel had ten children, six of whom survived, and names later sons Thomas Crichton, born 1853, and Henry, born 1857 and dying young.<ref name="Grenville">Grenville County Historical Society, [https://www.grenvillecountyarchives.ca/uploads/1/4/7/7/147712809/jul_aug_2023_the_grenville_sentine__1_.pdf ''The Grenville Sentinel'', July–August 2023], “The Glasgow House,” pp. 3–4.</ref> Those two later births plus the eight people appearing as children in 1851 form a coherent ten-child reconstruction, but original birth, baptism or estate records are still needed to prove each relationship.

The 1866–67 Fuller directory listed Samuel as a general dealer on King Street.<ref>[https://www.collectionscanada.gc.ca/obj/001075/f2/nlc008163.pdf ''Fuller's Counties of Leeds, Grenville, Lanark and Renfrew Directory for 1866 & 1867''], Prescott entry for Samuel Glasgow.</ref> The death-notice transcription published on 29 January 1867 said he had died at Prescott after becoming a successful merchant and left a widow and a wealthy family.<ref name="Sentinel" /> Local history dates his death to 1866 and identifies the family burial place as Sandy Hill Presbyterian Cemetery.<ref name="Grenville" />


Samuel was a brother of Robert Glasgow, the Prescott shipbuilder. Robert's will, dated 9 October 1849, gives one sixth each to his brothers Daniel, Samuel, John and Thomas, his sister Mary, and collectively the children of his brother James; it does not call James deceased.<ref name="RobertWill1849">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 35, registered will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated 9 October 1849, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S original image].</ref> Memorial 13 records a 30 October 1856 deed, registered 13 November 1856, by which Robert's widow Jane sold Samuel, merchant, property in which he held one undivided sixth share under Robert's will.<ref name="RobertWill1856">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 36, Memorial 13, dated 30 October 1856 and registered 13 November 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWYM-6 original image].</ref> Memorial 465, dated 30 July 1861 and registered 7 October, names Daniel of Kilrea, County Londonderry, watchmaker, and wife Margaret, and Thomas of Lisnagaver, County Antrim, farmer, and wife Mary Ann, in transfers to Samuel of two undivided sixth interests under Robert's will.<ref name="RobertWill1861">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200419, image 240, Memorial 465, registered 7 October 1861, printed p. 397, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D original image].</ref> The deeds establish the stated Daniel, Thomas and Samuel as Robert's brothers by place, trade and wife; they do not identify the siblings' parents.

A further conveyance identifies Samuel's widow by her recorded name. On 25 March 1868, registered 18 August, Alexander Glasco of Rochester, New York, express agent and son of James Glasco formerly of Prescott, carpenter, conveyed an undivided eighteenth interest to '''Mary Eno Glasgow''', widow of the late Samuel Glasgow, for $166.66.<ref name="AlexanderGlasco1868">Grenville County land records, DGS 8200420, image 120, C114, dated 25 March 1868 and registered 18 August 1868, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQRC-Y original image].</ref> Eno is a recorded name in this deed, not a proved maiden name. This Alexander has not been identified with [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] of Lisnagaver.

== Research Notes ==

A later title-chain account calls early Prescott shipbuilder Robert Glasgow Samuel's father, says Robert left his house to six children, and says Samuel bought his siblings' shares.<ref>[https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf Theresa Taylor, “Auction all for others,” ''Brockville Recorder & Times'', 22 February 2017].</ref> This is credible local-history evidence but not an inspected contemporary kinship record. Do not attach Robert until the underlying deed or estate file is read.

The original memorials correct that relationship: Robert was Samuel's brother, not his father. They do not establish that James the carpenter named in later deeds was Robert's brother, and the apparent share fractions require a full reading of Robert's will before a complete inheritance reconstruction is stated.<ref name="Recorder">Theresa Taylor, [https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf “Auction all for others,”] ''Brockville Recorder & Times'', 22 February 2017.</ref>

A derivative Leeds and Grenville estate index gives Samuel an estate year of 1875, conflicting with his reported 1866 death. The original file must be inspected to determine whether this is a delayed proceeding, a different man or an indexing error. The same derivative index gives James E. Glasgow an estate period of 1900–09, which likewise provides no identity, file number or contents.

The local One Tree export and public WikiTree indexing were searched again on 13 August 2026. No profile matches this Irish-born Prescott merchant. [[Glasgow-2908|Samuel Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] remained in Ireland in 1851 and is excluded. Other same-name profiles have incompatible places, ages or families.

=== Uncertain 1851 household transcriptions ===
The 1851 Prescott census transcription includes two child names read as Alba and Lycania Glasgow, and later tradition supplies a Robert born about 1835. The readings of Alba and Lycania are uncertain and have not been supported by separate records; they are retained as household research leads rather than newly created child profiles.<ref>[https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1851&op=img&id=e002351566 Underlying record source: alba glasgow].</ref><ref>[https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1851&op=img&id=e002351566 Underlying record source: lycania glasgow].</ref><ref>[https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf Underlying record source: robert glasgow].</ref>

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==

'''Nancy Glasgow''' was born about 1820–1821. She later lived at Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, where she died before January 1892, probably on 31 October 1891.

No record names Nancy's parents. The January 1892 probate citation lists children of John, Alexander and Robert Glasgow, Jane Dysart, Ann McClelland and Mary Thompson, and names David, James and Samuel Anderson at Gortahar among the cited heirs or next of kin. It does not name Elizabeth as their mother; her identification comes from other family records. The citation, Nancy's explicit niece and nephew statements in her will, and the Irish family records support a '''probable sibling network''' associated with Rasharkin parish, County Antrim. The notice does not expressly state every sibling relationship or establish that the list is complete.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

The '''John Glasgow, farmer''' named as father in the 1846 marriage of [[Glasgow-867|John Glasgow of Lisnagaver]] is a candidate for Nancy's father only if the proposed siblings shared that parent. Full and half-sibling relationships remain unresolved. The proposed father represented by [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow]] is not thereby identified with the 1796 Desertoghill flax-premium recipient. Nancy was earlier attached to [[Glasgow-3904|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Unknown-761034|Rosanna Unknown]]; that parentage remains unproved, but omission of Thomas's or Daniel's family from the citation does not disprove it. Neither their absence nor the probable sibling network establishes a replacement father. No mother has been identified.<ref name="NancyCitation" />

=== Plattsburgh and Will ===

On 15 January 1889 Nancy made her Last Will and Testament at Plattsburgh. In 1880, '''Nancy Glasgow''', age 65 and born in Ireland, was living in Plattsburgh with Delia A. Walworth and Alice C. Walworth; she was recorded as single, a servant, and "Other" in relation to the head of household. This repeated association helps explain Nancy’s later appointment of Hiram Walworth as executor and bequests to Walworth children. It strengthens the identification of the Plattsburgh Nancy, but it does not prove that she was related to Alexander Glasgow or to Mary and Ann.

<ref name="Nancy1860">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MC7C-HHK FamilySearch], U.S. census, 1860, Nancy Glascoe, The Village of Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, record MC7C-HHK, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
<ref name="Nancy1880">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:MZZF-HDJ FamilySearch], U.S. census, 1880, Nancy Glasgow, Plattsburgh, Clinton County, New York, record MZZF-HDJ, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>

=== Clinton County Probate Index and Petition Trail ===

FamilySearch's Clinton County probate index lists Nancy Glasgow with a death date of 31 October 1891, residence in Plattsburgh, and a testate estate; the representative is identified as Hiram Walworth. A separate FamilySearch transcript from the Clinton County guardianship and probate records for 1892–1898 records the estate as Nancy Glasgow, then lists a petition filed by Hiram Walworth as executor named for probate of the will, an order for citation, service by publication, filing of the executor's oath, probate of the will, and issuance of letters testamentary to Hiram Walworth. This confirms the probate trail and identifies the surviving record group most likely to contain the names of Nancy's heirs or next of kin. The available transcript is AI-generated and does not itself state Nancy's relationship to Alexander Glasgow; the original petition and service pages still need to be read.

<ref name="NancyProbateIndex">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33S7-9YCX-9W3 FamilySearch], Clinton County, New York, ''Probate Indexes 1807–1969, 1830–1969'', entry for Nancy Glasgow, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>
<ref name="NancyProbatePetition">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYCZ-X98 FamilySearch], Clinton County, New York, ''Guardianship Records 1892–1898, Probate Records 1892–1898'', transcript for estate of Nancy Glasgow, accessed 16 September 2026.</ref>


=== New contemporary death notice and age conflict ===

The ''Plattsburgh Sentinel'' of 6 November 1891 reports that Nancy died '''at Plattsburgh on 31 October 1891, aged about 75''', and that her funeral took place on Monday afternoon at the '''Peristrome Presbyterian church'''. This independently corroborates the cemetery transcription's death date. Its age implies birth about 1815–1816, whereas Nancy's own January 1889 will, saying about 68, implies about 1820–1821. Both are approximate; the discrepancy is unresolved. The maintained census indexes also give varying ages (30 in 1860, 50 in 1870 and 65 in 1880), so the two estimates are not proved birth-year bounds.<ref name="NancyDeathNotice1891">''Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 6 November 1891, p. 8, death notices, Nancy Glasgow; [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18911106-01.1.8 original newspaper page], original image inspected 29 September 2026.</ref>

The original probate docket records a special guardian for minor heirs, a collateral inheritance tax appraisal commissioned from Cabell McLean in March 1894, and his report filed 28 April 1894. It does not reproduce a kinship schedule. Robert Wallace Anderson, son of Nancy's deceased nephew Robert, supplies a younger beneficiary who could explain a guardian, but the ward is not named in the docket.<ref name="NancyDocketReview1894">Clinton County Surrogate's Court, probate minutes, vol. 6, p. 6, Nancy Glasgow estate; FamilySearch DGS 005115656, image 34, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:33SQ-GYCZ-X98 original docket]; visually inspected 29 September 2026. Exact March day and guardian's name not confidently read.</ref>

== Biography ==

'''Mary Glasgow''' married a man named '''Thompson''' and had children, but no record of her own birth, marriage or death has been located and her husband's forename is unknown.

She is identified by the probate citation in the estate of [[Glasgow-4070|Nancy Glasgow]] of Plattsburgh, New York. The citation, dated 14 January 1892, lists "the children of Mary Thompson whose names and places of residence are unknown" among Nancy's heirs and next of kin, in the same group as the children of John, Alexander and Robert Glasgow, of Jane (Glasgow) Dysart, of Elizabeth (Glasgow) Anderson (sons "living at Gortahar") and of Ann McClelland.<ref>''The Plattsburgh Sentinel'', 26 February 1892, p. 6 (citation dated 14 January 1892). [https://www.nyshistoricnewspapers.org/?a=d&d=plts18920226-01.1.6 newspaper page]; also printed in ''The Plattsburgh Republican'', 23 January–13 February 1892.</ref>

A New York probate citation of this period had to be directed to the testator's heirs and next of kin, so Mary was a deceased sister of Nancy — a daughter of the sibling group's father (see Research Notes).

== Research Notes ==

This is the thinnest of the sibling profiles. Mary is not named in any located Irish record; her LNAB Glasgow, her parentage and even her Irish residence are inferences from the probate citation. Her parents are reassessed as [[Glasgow-4090|John Glasgow, farmer]] (uncertain) and an unknown mother. No dates should be added without a record. A civil death of a Mary Thompson, widow of William Thompson, farmer, at Tannybrake, Connor parish, on 7 March 1888 aged 73 is an age-compatible candidate but is NOT proved to be this Mary.

current: {{Estimated Date}} [[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was an early shipbuilder at Prescott, Upper Canada, later Canada West. Prescott heritage material identifies him as the builder of the Centre Street house now known as Glasgow House.Town of Prescott, [https://www.prescott.ca/media/3dtiztjk/council-agenda-june-16-2025.pdf ''Council Agenda, 16 June 2025''], heritage-designation material for 388 Centre Street, “Glasgow House.” A later property history dates the building to about 1835.Theresa Taylor, [https://www.theresataylor.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/Auction-all-for-others-Brockville-Recorder.pdf “Auction all for others,”] ''Brockville Recorder & Times'', 22 February 2017. Robert made his will on 9 October 1849. The registered copy divides his estate into six shares: one each for his brothers Daniel, [[Glasgow-4010|Samuel]], John and Thomas Glasgow, one collectively for the children of his brother James, and one for his sister Mary Glasgow.FamilySearch, ''Land records of Grenville County, 1822–1955'', film 008200419, image 35, registered copy of the will of Robert Glasgow of Prescott, dated October 1849 and registered in 1856, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S image 3Q9M-CSLG-LWY9-S]; original image inspected 8 September 2026. The explicit sibling language makes Samuel Robert's brother, not his son. The later statement that Robert left the house to six “children” and that a son Samuel acquired the other shares appears to have misread the six-share title chain. Local history reports that Robert died at Prescott in 1856. The 1856 date is compatible with an 1849 will: 1849 is the date on which the will was made, while 1856 is the reported death and registration period. == Research Notes == === The 1842 census lead === A modern index reports a Robert Glasgow in Augusta in the 1842 Canada West census. The image formerly cited for that claim, frame 004569584_00050, was inspected at full resolution and contains no readable Robert Glasgow entry.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1842&op=img&id=004569584_00050 1842 Census of Canada West, image 004569584_00050], inspected 13 August 2026. It is not used here as evidence for Robert's identity. === Family interpretation === The will's named beneficiaries are Robert's siblings and the children of one brother. It does not name Robert's parents, spouse or children. The 30 July 1861 conveyance, B465, identifies the will’s Daniel as the Kilrea watchmaker and Thomas as the Lisnagaver farmer, with wives Margaret and Mary Anne. This establishes the Irish sibling identities when read with the will; it does not name their parents or identify Alexander of Lisnagaver as another brother.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LWB8-D Prescott land register, volume B, memorial 465, pp.397–398, DGS 008200419, images 240–241]. The 1861 deed identifies the brothers as [[Glasgow-3896|Daniel of Kilrea]] and [[Glasgow-987|Thomas of Lisnagaver]]. The original 15 September 1869 deed, C298, identifies the sister as Mary Black, formerly Glasgow, and names six children, including John and Rose Ann Black of Drumoolish.[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSLG-LQTY-K Prescott land register, volume C, memorial 298, pp.476–482, DGS 008200420, images 277–280]. John of Prescott, watchmaker, remains an unassigned profile identity. James the Prescott carpenter is a property-based comparison for brother James, but their identity is not yet proved; the will does not say James was deceased. Robert's actual birthplace is unknown. His birth is estimated only far enough before about 1835 for him to have worked as a shipbuilder and built the house. His brother Samuel was recorded as Irish-born in the original 1851 Prescott census.Library and Archives Canada, [https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item/?app=Census1851&op=img&id=e002351566 1851 Census of Canada West, Prescott, page 31, lines 11–18, image e002351566], Samuel Glasgow household. Ireland is therefore a usable uncertain creation-field location from Robert's documented immediate-family context; it is not a statement that Robert's birthplace has been found. Prescott should be entered as an uncertain death place from the local history, not as a birthplace. === Duplicate audit === The local One Tree export, current project index and live WikiTree name results were reviewed in August and September 2026. No compatible Prescott shipbuilder profile was found. [[Glasgow-1367|Robert Glasgow of Glenleslie]], [[Glasgow-1171|Robert Glasgow of New York]], [[Glasgow-1983|Robert Glasgow of South Carolina]], [[Glasgow-1189|Robert Glasgow of Ohio]] and [[Glasgow-2769|Robert Glasgow of Tennessee]] have incompatible documented lives. Create Robert unconnected; the sibling link to Samuel can be expressed in the biographies until their parents are identified. == Sources ==

== Biography ==
'''Mary Ellen Glasgow''' was born on 14 February 1867 at Lisnagaver, County Antrim, Ireland. Her mother was Mary Glasgow; no father was entered in the civil birth register. Ann Glasgow of Lisnagaver, who was present at the birth, informed the registration on 12 March 1867. The birth was registered in Dirraw district, Ballymoney union.<ref name="birth1867">General Register Office Ireland, births registered in 1867 in Dirraw district, Ballymoney union, County Antrim, printed page 6, entry 214, Mary Ellen; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1867/03501/2286677.pdf original register return, PDF page 1], [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/view?record_id=f66be225e5-6827480 IrishGenealogy record]; image inspected 30 September 2026.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

The GRONI birth index names Mary Glasgow and gives 17 February 1867 in the Ballymoney district, reference U/1867/31/1005/2/214.<ref>General Register Office for Northern Ireland (GRONI), civil birth index, Mary Glasgow, 17 February 1867, Ballymoney district, U/1867/31/1005/2/214; [https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/birth online index].</ref> The original return's entry 214 names Mary Ellen and clearly reads 14 February 1867.<ref name="birth1867" /> The matching district, year, numbered entry and February birth support identifying these as the same registration. The reason for the differing day in the index remains unresolved.

The mother may be [[Glasgow-3167|Mary Glasgow of Lisnagaver]], and the informant may be [[Glasgow-438|Ann Glasgow]], but these identifications require corroboration. The birth register does not state a relationship between the two women.<ref name="birth1867" />
